newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity called flat as supply increases.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity called flat as supply increases.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were called to open flat Wednesday as western power supply continued to rise as more generating units were put back into operation from recent outages.

August Palo Verde (PV) futures were quoted at $34.60-34.90 a megawatt hour (MWh) compared with Tuesday's settlement at $34.66, while August California-Oregon Border (COB) was talked at $21.60-21.85 against yesterday's close at $21.53.
The two San Onofre Nuclear Generating Station (SONGS) units in southern California reached startup mode Wednesday morning.
The 1,070 megawatt (MW) SONGS unit 2 was shut June 29 to replace its charge line check valves, and the adjoining 1,080 unit 3 was taken out of service April 12 for refueling.
Up in Richland, Washington, output at the 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant climbed to 73 percent earlier today.
In addition to more nuclear generation, the 550 MW unit 3 at the Jim Bridger coal-fired complex in Wyoming was expected to resume operation today.
On the downside, technical analysts expected August PV to test chart support at $34.00 and August COB 20.50.
Power futures may receive support from an early rise in daily cash prices amid unconfirmed reports of transmission line problem in the Southwest, market sources said.
Day-ahead power prices for firm, peak delivery to the Palo Verde switchyard in Arizona rose almost ten dollars to $47.00-50.00 a MWh, the sources said.
One West trader explained, "It may be an emotional response to the prices in the East."
Yesterday, prescheduled peak power for today in parts of the Midwest areas rocketed toward $200 a MWh.
Ongoing strength in natural gas futures was also expected to give cushion to the electricity complex, traders said.
NYMEX August Henry Hub natgas futures opened up 2.3 cents at $2.185 per million British thermal units.
Meteorologists called for normal temperatures to continue across the Pacific Northwest through next week, and hot but seasonal weather over most of the Southwest.
Although triple-digit heat would continue to bake inland cities like Phoenix and Las Vegas, gentler 70s-80s F readings are expected to hug the more highly populated coastal region.
Separately, southbound capacity of the AC segment of the Pacific Intertie transmission system will be cut by 250 MW to 3,200 MW between 0900 and 1600 PDT on Thursday and Friday for maintenance work.
